title: Roos complex computes inverse limit on K-injective towers
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with exact countable products and enough injectives, and let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be the abelian category of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system] in $\mathcal A$. Let $I_\bullet$ be a K-injective cochain complex of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$, i.e. every morphism of complexes from an acyclic complex of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ to $I_\bullet$ is homotopic to zero (the notion of [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], with $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ in place of the category of sheaves). Write $P=\prod_n\operatorname{ev}_n(I_\bullet)$ for the termwise product complex, $P^p=\prod_n(I_n)^p$, and let $1-s:P\to P$ be the chain map given in each degree by the transition endomorphism of the inverse system $((I_n)^p)_n$ [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Let $L^p=\varprojlim_n(I_n)^p$ be the termwise inverse limit, realized as $\ker(1-s:P^p\to P^p)$, with inclusion $\iota:L\to P$, and let $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ be the shifted mapping cone of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with terms $P^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Py-(1-s)x,\,d_Px)$. Then the canonical map $\eta:L\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, $\eta^p=(0,\iota^p)$, is a morphism of complexes and a quasi-isomorphism. Consequently $L$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ represent the same object of $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 070M (lemma-difficulty-K-injectives), using Tag 0BK6 (lemma-product-K-injective); the arbitrary-tower form is obtained by replacing a K-injective representative by a termwise injective one

proof.text: Apply Q to the squares and homotopies. Define v=Q(cU) inv(Q(etaJ)) Q(lR). The first square and kernel retraction imply Q(eta)v=id; the second square and cone retraction imply v Q(eta)=id. Thus Q(eta) is an isomorphism, and DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso proves eta is a quasi-isomorphism.

The item is for an arbitrary K-injective complex of towers, so the split was written: Steps 1-3 set up lim, prod, 1-s, the cone and the map eta, prove homotopy invariance and that 1-s is split epi on split towers (elementary); Step 4 gets the split-term case from the new node lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis; Step 5 replaces I by a quasi-isomorphic complex with split terms through the new node lem-weil-tower-split-envelope (Tow(A) levelwise by the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian); Step 6 uses K-injectivity through lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived to get a homotopy retraction r of u; Step 7 is the retract argument. Statement clarified (not changed in content): K-injective defined for Tow(A) explicitly (the cited definition node is for etale sheaves), L realized as ker(1-s), the cone and the map eta=(0,iota) written out. The hypotheses 'exact countable products' and 'enough injectives' are not used by the proof (only the existence of countable products); they are kept since the citer works in that setting.

lean.statement: theorem roosComplex_quasiIso (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A] [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A] [EnoughInjectives A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] (P L C : CochainComplex A ℤ) (eP : ∀ p : ℤ, P.X p ≅ ∏ᶜ (fun n : ℕ ↦ (I.X p).obj (Opposite.op n))) (hP : ∀ p q : ℤ, P.d p q ≫ (eP q).hom = (eP p).hom ≫ Limits.Pi.map (fun n ↦ (I.d p q).app (Opposite.op n))) (oneSubS : P ⟶ P) (hS : ∀ p : ℤ, oneSubS.f p = (eP p).hom ≫ towerTransitionEndomorphism (fun n ↦ (I.X p).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≫ (eP p).inv) (iota : L ⟶ P) (hKernel : ∀ p : ℤ, iota.f p ≫ oneSubS.f p = 0) (hL : ∀ p : ℤ, IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (iota.f p) (hKernel p))) (eC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.X (p + 1) ≅ P.X p ⊞ P.X (p + 1)) (hC : ∀ p : ℤ, C.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1) ≫ (eC (p + 1)).hom = (eC p).hom ≫ biprod.lift (-(biprod.fst ≫ P.d p (p + 1)) - biprod.snd ≫ oneSubS.f (p + 1)) (biprod.snd ≫ P.d (p + 1) (p + 1 + 1))) : ∃ eta : L ⟶ C, (∀ p : ℤ, eta.f (p + 1) ≫ (eC p).hom = biprod.lift 0 (iota.f (p + 1))) ∧ QuasiIso eta ∧ IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Q).map eta)
